newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar pulled up by retail, consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: India sugar pulled up by retail, consumer demand.

text.p: Consumer buying and retailer interest, coupled with low arrivals have pushed up sugar prices on the local market, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Fresh consumer buying as well as increased enquiries from retailers dragged prices upward while arrivals were low," one dealer said.
Sentiment stayed firm on the back of a hike in the price of sugar supplied through the public distribution system (PDS) by the Indian government.
"Government has raised selling price of PDS sugar from 9.05 rupees per kg to 10.50 rupees on Monday," one broker said.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5/10 rupees to 1,280/1,305 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose the same margin at 1,310/1,400 rupees per quintal.
"Supplies were low as most of the delivery tenders from mills out of the free sale quota for the first half of current month are exhausted," the broker said.
"Supply, however, will improve next week," he added.
